title: Section models for open and clopen integer-shift squares on ring diagrams
statement:
Let $C_1\leftarrow C_2\leftarrow\cdots$ be an inverse sequence of commutative rings. For a scheme $W$ choose a small skeleton of its pro-etale site and put $B_{n,W}=(C_n)_W$. Let $\mathscr S_W$ be the abelian category of strict semilinear module systems: objects are $B_{n,W}$-module sheaves $M_n$ with $B_{n+1,W}$-linear maps $M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{n+1,n}M_n$, and morphisms commute with transitions. Identify it with modules over $B_\bullet$ on the simultaneous ringed diagram site and use $D(\mathscr S_W)$, the ordinary unbounded derived category [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. For a scheme morphism $v$ let $P_v$ be exact termwise inverse image. For a complex $M$, use $M[r]^p=M^{p+r}$ with differential $(-1)^r d_M$, and give $P_v$ its termwise shift comparison.

For an open immersion $j$ use exact termwise extension by zero $J_j\dashv P_j$, normalized by the open unit which is identity on localized sections [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], and equip $J_j$ with termwise shifts. For every $v$ let $S_v$ be total right-derived system direct image, with the K-injective shift comparison, equivalently the mate of the termwise shift of $P_v$ under $P_v\dashv S_v$. For open immersions $s:U\hookrightarrow V'$ and $b:V'\hookrightarrow V$ set $k=b\circ s$. Let $c:J_bJ_s\cong J_k$ be the canonical extension compositor and let $\beta:P_bJ_k\cong J_s$ be the open-unit-normalized restriction identification.

There are simultaneous termwise complex representatives of $c$ and $\beta$, compatible with every coefficient transition and every integer shift. The compositor is the canonical transitivity identification of extensions by zero, with identity restriction to $U$ and zero on the complementary open wherever that description applies. The restriction identification has identity restriction to $U$; its inverse is precisely the $J_s\dashv P_s$ adjunct prescribed by the normalized open base-change comparison in [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] for $g=b$, $j=k$, $j'=s$, $g_U=1_U$. Its degree-$p$ representative on a shifted input $M[r]$ is the degree-$(p+r)$ representative on $M$.

If $s$ is also closed, put $Z=V'\setminus s(U)$. Restriction to $U$ and $Z$ gives a product decomposition $\mathscr S_{V'}\simeq\mathscr S_U\times\mathscr S_Z$ which extends to ordinary unbounded complexes and their derived categories. Under this decomposition $J_s$ is $N\mapsto(N,0)$, termwise direct image is the same exact functor, and its canonical comparison $\delta:J_s\cong S_s$ is the localized comparison from that exact functor to its total right-derived functor. The component projection $\pi_s:1\to J_sP_s$ is $(x,y)\mapsto(x,0)$. The comparison $\delta$ and the projection $\pi_s$ commute with the specified shifts, including the K-injective/mate normalization on $S_s$. In the proper/open square setting of [lem-sf-semilinear-proper-open-mate-pasting], these are exactly its clopen section comparison and component projection.

For $\tau=c,\beta,\delta,\pi_s$, every integer $r$, and every input $M$, one has $\chi_G\tau_{M[r]}=\tau_M[r]\chi_F$ for the composite operation shifts of its source and target. These are natural identities in the derived category of whole semilinear systems before any evaluation or scalar restriction, coherent for adding shifts and iterating open composition. They hold also for the empty open and for identity immersions; no boundedness, coefficient flatness, normalization or constructibility assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Apply the concrete witness constructed in [lem-sf-diagram-open-model-construction]. Use the existing additive exact ordinary open functors. Define the ordinary compositor by leftAdjointCompIso and the restriction by its inverse followed by the inverse open unit. The adjunction conjugacy unit identity proves both normalization formulas. Apply derivedMate_comparison with the exact-derived hom-equivalence factorization to identify the localized compositor and inverse restriction with the specified jComp and restrictionIso. All representatives are actual natural transformations of whole systems.

proof.text: For complementary opens, use uniqueness of section gluing to show the pair of ordinary restrictions is faithful. Exactness gives reflection of monomorphisms and epimorphisms, hence joint reflection of isomorphisms. Extension restricted to the other open is zero. The inverse to the pair of restrictions is the biproduct of the two extension functors; its unit is the pair of open units followed by biproduct inclusions, and its counit is the biproduct descent of the open counits. These are isomorphisms by the triangle identities, the cross-component zero identities and joint reflection. Repeat on complexes and on derived categories, where exact derived functors jointly reflect isomorphisms. The resulting insertion is normalized by the inverse open unit on the first component and the unique zero isomorphism on the second.

proof.text: Construct the ordinary map from extension to direct image from the direct-image unit and the inverse open unit. The existing clopen isomorphism and full faithfulness show this canonical map is invertible. Compare the exact-derived adjunction with the homotopy-localized adjunction by their unit factorization equations. Localization of the ordinary transpose then identifies the map with openToS followed by the canonical exact/right-derived comparison. Define the ordinary projection as the direct-image unit followed by the inverse canonical comparison. Its localization equals pi by the same unit factorization and cancellation. The adjunction triple identity gives its first component; the complementary component is uniquely zero.

proof.text: The degree and shifted-degree formulas of each termwise natural transformation are definitional; its chain shift square is the standard natural-transformation shift instance. The localized open adjunction units commute with the prescribed termwise shifts. The canonical right-derived adjunction commutes with the fixed K-injective shift. The explicit unit words for jComp, restrictionIso, openToS and pi therefore commute with those shifts. Use the existing compositor associativity. Prove ordinary direct-image identity laws from the uniquely normalized section formulas and the generic pullback-site identity equations. Transfer these laws to ordinary inverse images by adjunction mates, localize using the generic identity-descent lemmas, and transfer to extension identity laws through leftAdjointCompIso. No resolution is chosen and all equalities precede coefficient evaluation.
